c: Generic tests are not only for models. You can attach them to
with exactly the same syntax. These four (models, sources, seeds, snapshots) are the resources that can have data tests; an analysis, for example, cannot, because it is never built.
A source is data that dbt does not control. If a raw table suddenly contains duplicated ids, every model built on it is wrong. A test on the source catches the problem
, before it spreads, and the failure message points to the real culprit (the raw data), not to a model five steps later.

Here are the two singular tests of the reference project:

blocks.text:
-- Singular test: for every order, the amount in fct_orders must equal
--   (1) the sum of its 4 payment-method columns, and
--   (2) the sum of its successful payments in stg_stripe__payments.
-- The test FAILS if this query returns at least one row.

with

orders as (

    select * from {{ ref('fct_orders') }}

),

payments as (

    select
        order_id,
        sum(amount) as paid_amount
    from {{ ref('stg_stripe__payments') }}
    where status = 'success'
    group by order_id

)

select
    orders.order_id,
    orders.amount,
    orders.bank_transfer_amount + orders.coupon_amount
        + orders.credit_card_amount + orders.gift_card_amount as sum_of_methods,
    coalesce(payments.paid_amount, 0) as paid_amount

from orders
left join payments
    on orders.order_id = payments.order_id
where orders.amount <> orders.bank_transfer_amount + orders.coupon_amount
                       + orders.credit_card_amount + orders.gift_card_amount
   or orders.amount <> coalesce(payments.paid_amount, 0)
blocks.title: tests/assert_payments_match_order_totals.sql

blocks.text:
-- Singular test: when an order is paid, the payments must equal the total of
-- its order lines (quantity x unit price). Returns the orders that do not match.

with

items as (

    select
        order_id,
        sum(line_amount) as items_amount
    from {{ ref('fct_order_items') }}
    group by order_id

)

select
    orders.order_id,
    orders.amount,
    items.items_amount

from {{ ref('fct_orders') }} as orders
inner join items
    on orders.order_id = items.order_id
where orders.amount > 0
  and orders.amount <> items.items_amount

blocks.alt: Tests in the development workflow. Development: dbt build -s my_model+ after each change, before each commit. Then a pull request goes to CI: dbt build -s state:modified+ on every pull request; a failure blocks the merge. After the merge, the production job: dbt source freshness and dbt build, scheduled, with alerts on failure.
